name: German Red Cross (DRK) Refugee Relief Services
description: The German Red Cross (DRK) provides comprehensive relief services for refugees and asylum seekers in Germany, including reception and registration support, emergency accommodation, food distribution, medical first aid, psychosocial support, and family reunification tracing services. DRK operates in coordination with federal and state authorities at initial reception centers and community-level integration facilities across all 16 German states. Services include German language orientation, legal guidance referrals, and cultural mediation. DRK also runs specialized programs for unaccompanied minors and vulnerable groups such as pregnant women and persons with disabilities.
eligibility: Refugees, asylum seekers, and persons with tolerated status (Duldung) in Germany; services are available regardless of immigration status at emergency reception centers
amount: Free services (no monetary grant — direct assistance in kind)
applicationProcess: No formal application required for emergency services. Refugees can access DRK services at initial reception centers (Erstaufnahmeeinrichtungen) or contact local DRK chapters for community-level support. For family tracing, submit a request through the DRK tracing service (Suchdienst).
documentsRequired: No documents required for emergency reception services. For ongoing support programs, proof of asylum seeker status or registration certificate (Ankunftsnachweis) may be requested.

name: HIAS Europe — Refugee Legal and Integration Services
description: HIAS Europe provides legal assistance, social services, and integration support to refugees and asylum seekers across Europe. Operating in Greece, Austria, Poland, and other European countries, HIAS Europe offers free legal representation for asylum claims, legal counseling on family reunification, assistance with accessing national protection systems, psychosocial support, and community integration programs. HIAS engages pro bono attorneys and trained legal staff to represent refugees in proceedings and appeals. The organization also provides capacity-building for local civil society organizations and advocates for refugee-friendly policies at the EU level.
eligibility: Refugees, asylum seekers, and displaced persons in Europe; services are available regardless of religion, nationality, or ethnicity
amount: Free legal and social services (no monetary grant)
applicationProcess: Contact HIAS Europe through the website or visit a local HIAS office in Greece (Athens, Lesvos), Austria (Vienna), or Poland (Warsaw). Walk-in consultations available at field offices. Referrals also accepted from UNHCR and partner organizations.
geographicScope: Europe — primarily Greece, Austria, Poland, and advocacy at EU level
documentsRequired: Proof of identity (passport, ID card, or UNHCR registration); asylum registration documents if available; any existing legal correspondence related to asylum claim

name: IRAP — International Refugee Assistance Project (Europe)
description: The International Refugee Assistance Project (IRAP) provides free legal representation to refugees and displaced persons seeking safety through legal pathways in Europe and globally. IRAP's Europe office coordinates with a network of pro bono attorneys and law students to help refugees navigate complex European asylum systems, apply for family reunification, and access complementary protection pathways. The organization handles cases involving refugees from conflict zones including Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, and sub-Saharan Africa. IRAP also engages in strategic litigation and policy advocacy to expand legal protections for displaced persons across the European Union.
eligibility: Refugees and displaced persons seeking legal pathways to safety in Europe; priority given to individuals facing urgent protection needs including persecution, conflict, and gender-based violence
applicationProcess: Submit a legal assistance request through the IRAP website (refugeerights.org). Cases are screened and matched with pro bono attorneys. IRAP also accepts referrals from UNHCR, partner NGOs, and other legal aid organizations.
geographicScope: Europe-wide — with offices in Berlin and coordination across EU member states
documentsRequired: Proof of identity, documentation of persecution or conflict situation, any prior asylum correspondence or UNHCR registration; IRAP staff assist with document compilation

name: North Carolina DHHS Refugee Services Program
organization: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS)
description: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services Refugee Services Program provides a range of integration and resettlement support to refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, and other eligible immigrants in North Carolina. Services include employment assistance and job placement, English language training, transportation to appointments and services, interpretation and translation, case management, cultural orientation, and health screening referrals. The program works through a network of local nonprofit service providers across the state to deliver culturally and linguistically appropriate support during the critical first years after arrival.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders (SIVs), certified victims of trafficking, and other ORR-eligible populations residing in North Carolina; most services available for up to 5 years after arrival
amount: Free services; Refugee Cash Assistance up to $1,175/month for eligible individuals during first 12 months
applicationProcess: Contact your local resettlement agency in North Carolina or the NCDHHS Division of Social Services. Services are typically coordinated through the refugee's resettlement agency upon arrival. Self-referrals also accepted.
geographicScope: North Carolina — statewide through local nonprofit service provider network
documentsRequired: I-94 arrival record, proof of eligible immigration status (I-571, I-766, or ORR eligibility letter), Social Security card or application receipt, proof of North Carolina residency

name: New York OTDA BRIA — Refugee and Immigrant Assistance Programs
organization: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: The New York State Bureau of Refugee and Immigrant Assistance (BRIA) within OTDA administers a comprehensive suite of programs supporting newly arrived refugees and immigrants across New York State. Programs include Refugee Cash and Medical Assistance, employment services and vocational training, English language instruction (ESL/ESOL), transportation assistance to job sites and service appointments, youth mentoring and afterschool programs, elderly refugee services, and targeted services for survivors of torture. BRIA coordinates with over 40 local service providers and resettlement agencies throughout New York to deliver culturally appropriate assistance.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Amerasians, Special Immigrant Visa holders, certified trafficking victims, and Afghan/Ukrainian humanitarian parolees residing in New York State; most services available during first 5 years, some employment services up to 5 years
amount: Refugee Cash Assistance up to $1,202/month for singles (varies by household size) during first 12 months; additional employment and training services at no cost
applicationProcess: Contact your designated local resettlement agency in New York or call OTDA's refugee assistance helpline. Refugees are typically enrolled in BRIA programs upon arrival through their resettlement agency. Walk-in assistance available at many provider locations.
geographicScope: New York State — statewide, with primary service centers in New York City, Buffalo, Syracuse, Albany, and Utica
documentsRequired: I-94 arrival record, proof of eligible immigration status, Social Security number or application receipt, proof of New York State residency, income documentation

name: Washington State DSHS Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA)
organization: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS)
description: Washington State's Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program provides monthly cash assistance to eligible refugees and immigrants who do not qualify for other federal cash assistance programs such as TANF or SSI. Administered by the Washington DSHS through local Community Services Offices, RCA helps cover basic needs including food, housing, transportation, and personal necessities during the critical first months after resettlement. The program also connects recipients with employment services, job readiness training, and community resources. Washington State has historically been one of the top refugee resettlement states, with significant populations in the Seattle, Tacoma, and Spokane metro areas.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Amerasians, Special Immigrant Visa holders, and certified trafficking victims who arrived in the US within the past 12 months and do not qualify for TANF or SSI; must be a Washington State resident
amount: Up to $428/month for an individual; varies by household size and county
applicationProcess: Apply at your local DSHS Community Services Office (CSO) or through your resettlement agency. Applications can also be submitted online through Washington Connection (washingtonconnection.org). Processing typically takes 30 days.
geographicScope: Washington State — statewide through DSHS Community Services Offices
documentsRequired: I-94 arrival record, proof of eligible immigration status (I-571, I-766, or ORR eligibility letter), Social Security card or application receipt, proof of Washington State residency, income verification
